hypothesis: A signed perp-only exposure opposite to previously settled financing flow can improve net economics over a constant SHORT direction under the same risk policy. It is not a price trend/rank/selector or cash-spot hedge.
candidate: CORE5 direction = -sign(mean of 21 complete UTC daily raw settled-rate sums); every input day becomes available at its end plus one full UTC day; exactly zero or UNKNOWN input means CASH for that asset.
daily_funding_coverage: Actual event timestamps/rates/hours; 24 interval hours, finite original rates, positive hours, consecutive settlements and day-edge alignment within existing 60s archive jitter tolerance. Missing day is UNKNOWN, never observed zero.
control: Constant SHORT direction per CORE5 asset with same price eligibility and risk controller. No past-funding exit or annual fit.
raw_allocation: 0.12 per noncash asset, no redistribution of missing funding slots; original past30 daily simple-return annual covariance, original risk.scale annual10%, asset30%, gross60%. Same policy is not matched realized risk.
